registry_entry.why: ``default`` is a literal applied when the caller omits the parameter, so a bound whose value depends on today -- intrinio's one-year window, filled in transform_query when the caller names no dates (historical_dividends.py:74-78) -- has no field to be written in. The declaration sends no bound instead, which is a wider answer than the upstream one.

rows.notes: Single GET /securities/{symbol}/prices/adjustments, rows under 'stock_price_adjustments' (:95); no pagination loop. field_rename_map comes from the alias dict at :36-40 (date->ex_dividend_date, dividend->amount, dividend_currency->currency) restated as ColumnSpec.source_key; param_value_mapping from limit->page_size with default 100 at :25-30 as ParamSpec.query_key; derived_columns from the per-row stamping of the queried symbol at :102-104, now carried by ModelSpec.column_derives (DerivePlan source_kind=parameter). transform_query's 1-year relative default window (historical_dividends.py:74-78) fills a bound from today when the caller names none, while ParamSpec.default holds a literal, so the row needs relative_date_default (param.relative_default, absent): with an omitted bound this declaration sends no window and answers wider than upstream. That is the blocker and why the flag is false; the other three labels are each carried in specs.py and proven offline, so the row is one capability from ready, not three. tests/test_intrinio_engine_provider.py::TestHistoricalDividends proves symbol-stamped, renamed rows come out offline.
